title: Investigating Structural Transformations During Nanoparticle Oxidation in an Environmental TEM
content: The use of environmental transmission electron microscopy (ETEM) to observe real-time structural and compositional changes has proven to be a valuable tool for understanding the dynamic behavior of nanomaterials. However, even with aberration correction the introduction of a gaseous environment and elevated temperatures, as well as the associated sample drift, can reduce the image resolution and subsequent information transfer. Therefore, identifying the phase transformation of nanoparticles typically requires an obvious change in position, size, or structure. Compositional changes often result in subtle volume changes only, so elucidating mechanisms in real-time requires atomic-scale resolution or in-situ electron energy loss spectroscopy (EELS), which may not be widely accessible.
